source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'PWR_GB_GPU1_M~PWR_GB_GPU8_M' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES sends the complete GPU1_M-to-GPU8_M expression as one literal sensor name, which cannot prove eight records. It does not define `_M`, distinguish this family from the adjacent non-M GPU power family, establish stable GPU/component identity or identify the measured electrical boundary and averaging window.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires suffix decoding, eight separate records and a power-quantity definition. V3.1 additionally treats `_M` only as a possible module-channel cue from related rows—not as proof of memory or any particular rail—and requires explicit separation from the non-M family, a controller-channel map and synchronized measurement windows.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 898/2291 accepts the literal range command and output presence without decoding `_M`, resolving eight physical GPU/component identities, separating the non-M family or proving measurement-boundary/specification equivalence.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00083-V003 applies GPU driver/load and threshold behavior to the same labels and calls the stimulated target a module; that supports asking whether `_M` is a module channel but does not prove its exact electrical meaning or authorize workload here. Wistron-BMC-00188-V003 is the adjacent non-M family and must remain separate. Wistron-BMC-00989-V002 uses `PWR_GB_GPU1~8_M` with a source selector conflict and likewise cannot define this row.

historical_reviews.v3: The pilot/V3 review for the dynamic Wistron-BMC-00083-V003 case retained load/threshold coverage behind approval; it is related evidence only and does not convert this passive Sensor Page row into a stress test.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the exact `_M` labels; ED-34 treats suffix meaning, GPU topology, measurement boundary, controller channel, specification and tool as readiness inputs; ED-35 keeps this Sensor Page review passive without GPU load, policy, reset or firmware changes; ED-38 requires protected complete evidence, no clear/write/retry and engineer-owned verdict. Wistron I2C/I3C ownership keeps board-monitor access in BMC/platform-management scope unless Project SPEC says otherwise.

original_test_intent: Verify `PWR_GB_GPU1_M` through `PWR_GB_GPU8_M` are eight individually displayed BMC GPU-related power telemetry records in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, with the Project-defined `_M` meaning, physical GPU/component identity, electrical measurement boundary, quantity/units, status and supported thresholds for the recorded passive operating state.
original_method: Resolve the `_M` family definition, bind each index to a physical GPU and exact module/rail/board-monitor channel, then compare complete passive raw and UI readings with boundary-specific Project limits using aligned timestamps and averaging windows. Preserve GPU, BMC and log state; this row does not authorize the dynamic load/threshold stimulus from the related Assert-DeAssert case.
manual_activity: The GPU/baseboard power owner defines `_M`, maps all eight names to physical GPUs/components and stable UUID/BDF identities, identifies the exact monitor channels and supplies boundary-specific acceptance. Automation can collect passive BMC/GPU inventory and UI evidence; a human confirms the current operating context and owns the verdict. No GPU stimulus or policy change is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS and authoritative `_M` versus non-M family definition
Per-index physical GPU position, component/module identity, GPU PN/serial/UUID/BDF/VBIOS/FW and present/powered state
Per-sensor measured electrical boundary, quantity/units and power-monitor controller/bus/mux/address/channel/register
Scaling, accuracy, averaging/integration window, polling and cross-interface time-alignment rules
Stable SDR/UI identities plus boundary-specific tolerance, limits, thresholds/hysteresis, status and unavailable/stale behavior
Recorded GPU driver/persistence state, clocks, power cap, processes/workload, fan/inlet/airflow and any proposed equivalent host telemetry field
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel, NVIDIA XID or power/thermal logs; the Master clear instruction is preserved but excluded because existing state is relevant evidence and clearing is unnecessary for this passive check.
Do not issue `sensor get 'PWR_GB_GPU1_M~PWR_GB_GPU8_M'` as a wildcard. Enumerate and query eight exact records separately.
Do not infer `_M` means memory, motherboard or module from the suffix alone. The related dynamic row's word `module` is a cue requiring Project confirmation, not a definition.
Do not map GPU number from `nvidia-smi` index or BDF order without the approved physical/UUID topology, and do not substitute the adjacent non-M family.
Do not compare BMC module/rail power with NVIDIA device power unless the same electrical boundary and synchronized integration window are proven; plausible numeric agreement is not equivalence.
Do not start GPU workload, enable persistence, change clocks or power caps, reset/power-cycle/reseat a GPU, alter thresholds or flash firmware. Record the existing passive state.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/swapped GPUs, stale telemetry or BMC/UI/GPU disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the `_M` definition, its distinction from non-M, the eight-GPU/component/monitor-channel map, target, protected client, vendor reference and Script; build an eight-row expectation matrix.

Retrieve every `_M` record separately with full SDR/controller identity, electrical boundary, value, units, threshold capability, status, integration window and timestamp; capture each unchanged UI row.
Record simultaneous GPU inventory, present/power state, clocks/cap, processes/workload and cooling. Use host telemetry only as corroboration after boundary and window equivalence is approved.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, GPU load/policy/cap/clock/reset/power/service, threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define `_M` and approve the separate GPU1_M-to-GPU8_M physical/component and monitor-channel map without merging it with the non-M family.
Provide boundary-specific scaling/window, tolerance, limits/thresholds, status/freshness and absent/powered-off rules; approve any telemetry equivalence and tool/Script.
Review all eight `_M` points independently and issue the formal verdict without substituting aggregate, non-M, host-device or dynamic-stress evidence.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and a single response cannot prove eight records. It omits `_M` semantics, stable GPU/component identity, electrical boundary, monitor source and sampling-window mapping; its fallback is truncated, credential-exposing and cipher-assumptive.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate eight exact `_M` records, bind each to the approved physical GPU/component and board-monitor field, query through protected read-only access, and correlate complete synchronized UI/state evidence with the correct boundary-specific specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PWR_GB_GPU1_M through PWR_GB_GPU8_M, both WebUI paths, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or borrowing workload from another case.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an eight-row matrix keyed by physical GPU/component, stable UUID/BDF and exact monitor channel; document what `_M` measures, its difference from non-M and its integration window, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with boundary-specific rules under the unchanged passive state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact eight-GPU baseboard population and BMC/power-monitor/SDR/WebUI implementation documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/GPU-baseboard, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, GPU VBIOS/FW/driver, monitor firmware, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: GPU-baseboard power tree and `_M` label definition, GPU inventory/topology, monitor-controller specification, BMC SDR/telemetry definition, GPU power-policy recipe and WebUI schema.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the ambiguous `_M` range into eight stable component- and electrical-boundary-bound records, explicitly separates non-M, and adds synchronized state/window evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static `_M` display does not validate dynamic load response, threshold assertion/deassertion, fan/throttle/shutdown protection, performance per watt, power-cap enforcement, rail transients or the non-M family.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Authoritative `_M` meaning, eight-GPU/component/monitor map, state-specific acceptance, synchronized passive timing, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: GPU enumeration is unstable; module, rail, board-input and device telemetry can legitimately differ because of conversion losses, auxiliary loads and sampling windows, while powered-off devices may report zero or unavailable by design.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM, monitor-vendor or NVIDIA telemetry as an approved alternative or corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/boundary/window and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate GPU1_M-to-GPU8_M identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. Non-M or aggregate GPU power is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/GPU-baseboard/BIOS/BMC identity and eight-row physical position, component/module identity, GPU PN/serial/UUID/BDF/VBIOS/FW/presence/power-state map
Authoritative `_M` definition and explicit non-M distinction plus each electrical boundary and monitor controller/bus/mux/address/channel/register/scaling/window map
Complete separate raw values with stable IDs, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and synchronized timestamps plus redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Recorded driver/persistence/clocks/cap/processes/workload, fan/inlet/airflow and boundary/time-aligned Project/vendor comparison with any approved telemetry equivalence

Explicit missing/swapped/powered-off/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool evidence, no-clear/no-load-or-policy-change/no-retry proof, final GPU/BMC health and engineer-owned eight-point verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The `_M` suffix and electrical boundary are underdefined, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive display/specification validation of eight power records. Project definition can distinguish `_M` from non-M; this is execution readiness rather than a contradiction in the core purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The eight-point passive GPU-related power-display purpose is identifiable. Project topology and power-monitor documentation can supply suffix, boundary and acceptance details, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE and replaces one literal range query with eight stable GPU/component/electrical-boundary checks.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification and strengthens it with an explicit non-M separation, cautious module-channel interpretation, stable UUID/BDF identity, controller source and integration-window alignment.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with complete suffix/component/boundary/UI/spec evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Uses the Assert-DeAssert module wording only as a question to resolve; keeps dynamic stimulus, non-M and later list-parity coverage separate.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence or case identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an invalid range query, guessed `_M` meaning, unstable GPU index, wrong electrical boundary, non-M substitution or borrowed stress evidence from being presented as eight valid passive GPU-module power records.
independent_technical_reasoning: The paired use of `_M` in both GPU temperature and power families, plus the related dynamic row's instruction to stress the module, makes a module-associated channel plausible but does not establish memory, module input, rail or board-controller semantics. Power equivalence requires stable identity, electrical boundary, scaling and averaging-window alignment. This passive UI row therefore needs Project definitions and complete eight-point collection, but it must not trigger GPU load or inherit the dynamic case's protection coverage.
